topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecturer, frames the lecture series on cancer biology, and outlines the key learning outcomes regarding cancer causation.

topics.label: Cancer Etiology: Endogenous Factors, Genetics, and Environmental Epidemiology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the conceptual basis of cancer development by examining how intrinsic mutational processes, inherited genetics, and environmental exposures interact to drive cancer incidence across populations.

topics.label: Pathogens and Infectious Agents in Cancer Etiology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how viral, bacterial, and parasitic pathogens promote malignancy, using the multi-factorial etiology of Burkitt lymphoma as a primary case study.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Chemical and Physical Mutagenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the molecular mechanisms by which dietary, environmental, and physical mutagens undergo metabolic activation to form DNA adducts and induce genetic mutations.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion, Inflammatory Microenvironments, and Host Susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how non-mutagenic factors promote cancer growth through chronic inflammation and cellular signaling, highlighting the interplay between tumor promotion, tissue context, and host developmental timing.

topics.label: Methodologies for Determining and Proving Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics review the genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro experimental methodologies employed to identify carcinogens, assess mutational signatures, and weigh carcinogenic risks.
